_comment: Catalog of all static UI strings in the project. Algorithm explainer card text (managed in src/lib/algorithm-explainer/algorithms/*.json) is excluded. Organized by usage (component/area). Placeholders use {name} format.

infoTooltip.title: Training Metrics
infoTooltip.content: Metric values at the current step. Click a chip to toggle a metric in the chart.

detailPanel.emptyState: Click a step on the radial chart
detailPanel.noResponses: No response data for this step

infoTooltip.title: Optimization Objectives
infoTooltip.content: The PO update is computed in two stages: per-token contributions are aggregated into a single step-level scalar, then the policy moves one gradient step in the direction that maximizes it.

tokenLevel.label: Token-level Objective
tokenLevel.description: How each token contributes to the model update.

stepLevel.label: Step-level Objective
stepLevel.description: The token-level objectives are aggregated into a single value. The model takes one update step in the direction that maximizes it.

rolloutTooltip.title: Rollout Cycle
rolloutTooltip.content: A rollout cycle is one set of generated responses that the policy trains on. PO can take multiple gradient steps on the same rollouts — the policy isn't generating during these steps, only running inference to recompute log-probs, which makes the importance sampling ratio drift away from 1.

infoTooltip.title: Response Examples
infoTooltip.content: Sampled responses (rollouts) from the policy. Each row shows one response, color-coded by per-token contribution to the optimization update.

tooltip.title: Reward
tooltip.content: Scalar score given by the reward model for this response. In PO, this is the primary training signal — advantage = (reward − baseline).
tooltip.hint: Higher reward → more likely to be reinforced.

responseTooltip.title: Response {n}
responseTooltip.content: One sampled response from the policy for this prompt.

metrics._usage: Chart ring labels, chip label/popover (RadialChart.svelte), step metric panel tooltip (StepMetrics.svelte)

reward.def: Mean reward over a step group (or batch). Scalar score for the policy's responses.
reward.hint: Expect an upward trend when training is going well.

reward_std.def: Std of rewards within a step group (group_reward_std in GRPO).
reward_std.hint: If 0, all responses in the group got the same reward — advantage collapses to 0, no learning signal.

policy_objective.def: Policy objective the optimizer is maximizing (sign-flipped policy loss). PPO/GRPO/DAPO surrogate after clipping.
policy_objective.hint: Upward trend = policy improvement on the current batch.

policy_loss.def: PPO/GRPO surrogate loss. Moving toward negative values means the policy is improving.
policy_loss.hint: Small magnitude (near 0) is stable. Large swings are a blow-up signal.

learning_rate.hint: Typically flat after warmup, or follows a decay schedule.

response_length.def: Mean number of tokens in a response.
response_length.hint: Longer = more exploration. Sudden spikes may signal reward hacking.

kl.def: Mean KL divergence between current policy π and reference policy π_ref.
kl.hint: If too large, the policy drifts far from the reference — risk of collapse.

ref_kl.def: Reference-model KL (near-synonym of kl, named differently by some sources).

clip_fraction.def: Fraction of tokens whose PPO ratio fell outside the clip range.
clip_fraction.hint: If too high, consider adjusting learning rate or clip_eps.

grad_norm.def: Gradient norm of the parameter update.
grad_norm.hint: Spikes indicate instability. Clipping with max_norm is recommended.

entropy.def: Mean entropy of the policy distribution.
entropy.hint: Dropping too quickly means insufficient exploration.

value_loss.def: Regression loss of the critic (value function). PPO only.

total_loss.def: Sum of policy + value + entropy regularization.

advantage_mean.hint: Near 0 is normal. A strong skew to one side suggests a normalization issue.

advantage_std.def: Std of advantages within the batch.

return.def: Mean cumulative/discounted return. In GRPO it's nearly identical to advantage.

importance_sampling_ratio.def: Mean Importance Sampling ratio = exp(log_prob − old_log_prob).
importance_sampling_ratio.hint: Drifting far from 1.0 breaks the on-policy assumption.

dynamic_sampling_pass_rate.def: Percentage of samples that passed DAPO dynamic sampling.
dynamic_sampling_pass_rate.hint: Near 100% = filter too loose. Near 0% = too strict.

baseline.def: REINFORCE baseline b — running estimate of expected reward (EMA). Subtracted from reward to form advantage = r − b.
baseline.hint: Tracks reward closely. Used for variance reduction in REINFORCE.
